title: Space & Defense Daily — Monday, Nov 9, 2026
summary: A new Democratic Congress looks set to rein in and likely rename Golden Dome, with space-based interceptors most at risk; NATO is about €7 billion short on its 2026 Ukraine aid pledge as Europe rehearses a postwar Ukraine force in Poland and heads to the Abu Dhabi talks; NASA launched CLPS 2, a $10 billion lunar lander contract with eight companies, plus a nuclear-powered rover and about $1.3 billion in transport task orders.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Friday, Nov 6, 2026
summary: Space Force may need ~$1B in translator satellites because SpaceX’s SDN Backbone lasers can’t talk to SDA and SSC missile-warning birds; NATO opened a counter-drone marketplace and begins German-led drills in Lithuania as France extends Black Sea maritime patrols; Europe nears a Nov. 30 pick between HYDIS and HYDEF hypersonic interceptors.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Thursday, Nov 5, 2026
summary: NATO is drafting deep-strike plans against Russian bases and industry if alliance territory is attacked; Brussels hosts EU and NATO talks with the US, UK, France and Germany on Ukraine security guarantees ahead of Abu Dhabi; Space Force leaders say they tracked a Russian satellite near an ICEYE commercial SAR spacecraft and warn midterm budget delays could slow Guardian growth.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026
summary: Russia hits Ukraine's grid with its biggest energy strike of the year as NATO and the US, UK, France and Germany meet in Brussels on security guarantees; a leaked EU work programme says Europe's 2030 defence-readiness goal is at risk; the Space Force stands up a special operations component and seeks up to five cislunar seed satellites.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Tuesday, Nov 3, 2026
summary: Russia's widening strikes in the Black Sea near Romania and Bulgaria are testing how far NATO will let things go. The US approved a $2.1B sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, paid for by allies, though deliveries may not come until the 2030s. A coalition led by the UK and France will rehearse a postwar force for Ukraine in Poland from Nov 9 to 22.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Monday, Nov 2, 2026
summary: The US approved a $2.1B sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, paid for by allies, though deliveries may not arrive until after 2030. Drones entered Romania again on Oct 31, and sea-drone strikes on Black Sea shipping are continuing. Google is reportedly in early talks to help secure the data behind Golden Dome.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Friday, Oct 30, 2026
summary: The EU opened a €21.3 billion second round of SAFE defence loans. The US Army picked Lockheed Martin for its Future Interceptor program, worth more than $1 billion. NATO's Black Sea allies condemned drone attacks on shipping after another vessel was hit off Bulgaria.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Thursday, Oct 29, 2026
summary: The EU approved Hungary's €5.4bn loan, which closes the first round of its €150bn SAFE defence-loan program, and about €21bn is left for a second round open to all 27 member states. The UK says it will reach 3% of GDP on defense by 2030. ULA's Vulcan rocket returns to flight Nov. 13 with Amazon Leo satellites after nine months on the ground.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Wednesday, Oct 28, 2026
summary: The US picked Poland to host Europe's first PAC-3 Patriot interceptor maintenance hub, and the DIA says China's satellite fleet has tripled since 2018. Also, the UK, Netherlands, Finland and Poland are starting treaty talks on a joint defense procurement mechanism after the UK decided not to join Canada's defense bank.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Tuesday, Oct 27, 2026
summary: Europe's five biggest military powers pledged to carry more of NATO's load. Republican defense hawks warned that Trump's tilt toward Russia could sink his $1.5 trillion defense budget. And ESA ordered four more Galileo satellites.

title: Space & Defense Daily — Monday, Oct 26, 2026
summary: SpaceX restored full Starlink and Starshield service to Ukraine, though Musk still says Kyiv broke the terms of service. NASA laid out its plan for a crewed Moon landing in 2028. And the Space Force moved a missile-warning satellite and a cislunar mission off ULA's Vulcan onto SpaceX's Falcon Heavy.

title: Space & Defense Daily, Oct 23 to 25, 2026
summary: A fight between Ukraine and Musk over Starlink, which is pushing Europe toward its own military satellite communications; Russia-linked drone attacks on Black Sea shipping, which are pushing NATO to harden its eastern flank; and the US Space Force moving missile-warning, GPS, and cislunar launches from ULA's delayed Vulcan rocket to SpaceX.
